ambiguity_notes: Rev4 matches the March 2020 post. SI-2(2) concerns automated determination of remediation status, not automated installation. Explaining whether a script is an automated mechanism does not require si-2.2_prm_1 (frequency). The catalog alone cannot approve this MUSA implementation or determine whether its monthly/on-demand schedule satisfies the applicable profile.

Changed rev5 to rev4: the March 2020 post quotes Rev4 guidance and predates the final Rev5 publication. The statement and guidance explain separate execution domains and address spaces. Neither has an ODP. Windows/AWS configuration evidence, inheritance and assessor acceptance require deployment and assessment evidence beyond the catalog.

Restored the omitted i-Assure LOW-availability template quotation and final applicability question. Retained Rev4. Reduced required evidence to CP-7a: equipment and equivalent safeguards in b/c are not needed to decide whether CP-7 is applicable. Baseline selection/tailoring is outside the clause store. Neither recovery operations nor recovery time is needed for this applicability explanation. Updated question_sha256 after restoring the source.

Changed rev5 to rev4 using the June 2020 date and no stated draft-version intent. Changed ambiguous to full: the request is a clear pointer to service-account coverage. AC-2 guidance explicitly lists service accounts and AC-2a places account types under account management. IA-5 may support authenticator questions but is not an additional required mapping here. No actual account-type assignment is needed to locate the governing control.

Retained Rev4 because the original quotation uses its wording, despite publication shortly after final Rev5. COTS use does not itself establish control satisfaction or inheritance. Duties include safe message content and restricted disclosure. Identifying the actual si-11_prm_1 personnel/roles is unnecessary to explain responsibility; deployment configuration and contractual allocation remain outside the catalog.

Explicit Rev5 request for a downloadable, filterable low/moderate/high baseline spreadsheet. The clause store cannot supply that artifact or baseline membership. SP 800-53B and NIST supplemental spreadsheets are separate sources. No catalog ODP judgment applies.

Explicit Rev5. Replaced the PL-2a introductory fragment with substantive component, dependency and control-implementation clauses. Removed AC-2 as a required duty: AC-2/AC-6 are examples in the boundary question. Explaining external-service oversight does not require the concrete sa-09_odp.01 control list. Actual boundary, responsibility allocation and inherited coverage require RMF/service-specific evidence.

The request compares a control catalog with FedRAMP authorization and asks whether a Moderate control set is sufficient. FedRAMP program requirements, baselines and additional obligations are outside the clause store. Rev5 is retained as the review reference; the post does not state a revision. No catalog ODP list can resolve the program-level question.

Rev5 retained as the review reference; no revision is stated. Added AU-3 because AU-12c requires audit-record content. This asks for actual logging rules, so the answer needs available event types, selected events plus logging frequency/conditions, and audit-generating components. These inputs are absent. The catalog provides those duties, not Kiwi/OS settings or a complete compliance determination. Holding CUI alone does not establish the applicable framework.

Control selection for the stated SCIF/classified-system context and DISA/DAAPM process needs the governing baseline, categorization and agency/sponsor direction outside this clause store. Do not substitute generic NIST controls for those authorities. Rev5 is a review reference, not a confirmed revision in the post. No catalog ODP judgment applies.

Explicit Rev5. Two duty groups: select one or more of block, quarantine, or an organization-defined action; AND send an alert. The custom action is conditional on choosing that option, not an additional mandatory third duty. Read si-03_odp.04/.05/.06 definitions to resolve the syntax. No organization-specific response or recipient value is needed to explain the grouping. Scan frequency is outside the question.

Restored the source's closing 'Thank you.' and updated question_sha256. Explicit Rev5 clauses distinguish user-session termination from network disconnect. The question asks for acceptable concrete time limits, so applicable organizational trigger/time values are needed; 364 days is only a hypothetical. The catalog sets no universal maximum and cannot approve that value. Risk justification, imposed limits, 800-171 and legal definitions need external evidence.

Explicit Rev5 request for an authoritative PCI DSS crosswalk. This requires a published mapping and the applicable PCI DSS version, not isolated NIST clauses. The clause store is not a cross-framework mapping. No catalog ODP judgment applies.

Rev5 retained as the review reference; the post does not state a revision. Added SI-2d for tracking remediation through configuration management and SI-2 guidance for software/firmware scope. A flaw need not have a CVE. No remediation deadline is requested, so SI-2's update-time ODP is unnecessary. Vendor-specific outage mitigations and automated bug-tracking tools require information beyond the catalog.

The requested methodology/template for assigning control subsets to categories of systems is outside the clause store. It needs scoping, categorization, baseline/tailoring or overlay guidance and system context. A web-server label alone is not a control-family assignment. Rev5 is retained as the review reference; the post does not name a revision. No catalog ODP judgment applies.

Restored the omitted AU-4/AU-11 comparison, example-values request and ending; updated question_sha256. AU-4's placeholder means retention requirements, not TB capacity or TB/day generation rate. AU-11 sets the retention period; AU-4 sizes capacity to meet it. Added PL-2a.12 for recording tailoring rationale. Explaining these types does not need the organization's actual period. Do not endorse 60 days as its policy. External example-value documents remain outside the clause store.

Explicit Rev5. Expanded CA-2b to its scope/procedure/team clauses and added CA-2e, which requires a report of findings. The catalog supports an assessment plan and reporting, but a complete method and appropriate examine/interview/test procedures require SP 800-53A and the actual assessment scope. The question concerns workflow, not scheduling, so ca-02_odp.01 frequency is not required.

Rev5 retained as the review reference; no revision is stated. AC-10 covers concurrent sessions per account/account type, not only administrators and not necessarily one session. A clearly hypothetical limit can illustrate the rule without actual ac-10_odp.01/.02 assignments. Experiences and feasibility in the poster's ERP environment need external evidence. Explaining the control does not require configuring that environment.

The AC-2a quotation matches Rev5. Replaced introductory fragments with actual policy-content and SSP implementation/rationale clauses. AC-1 guidance explicitly says restating controls is not an organizational policy/procedure. Policy, procedure and SSP roles can be explained without choosing ac-01_odp.03 or any account list. FedRAMP acceptance and the final organization-specific document require additional evidence. Eramba reply text remains excluded.

Explicit Rev5 source links. AC-2(5) requires user logout when defined conditions apply; device lock under AC-11 does not itself end the session. The catalog does not universally require end-of-day logout. No actual trigger or lock timeout is needed to explain that distinction. Preserve the catalog's misleading AC-11 cross-reference in AC-2(5) guidance; it does not make lock and logout equivalent.
